walkthrough--agent-session--poster.title: An agent makes a reel over MCP (poster)

agent-session.proves: An agent (Claude Code, claude-sonnet-5-5) drives the studio over MCP from one prompt: list_templates, create_project, validate_project, render_project, get_job until done, get_render_output, and the studio renders a 9 s reel with 4 engines (remotion, motion-canvas, html, hyperframes).

steps.text: Claude Code starts with only the reelforge MCP tools allowed and the prompt
list_templates → 4 templates: kinetic-title (remotion), animated-explainer (motion-canvas), html-title (html), hyperframes-title (hyperframes)
create_project (manifest "One reel, four engines": 4 scenes, 1080x1920 @ 30 fps (remotion/kineti…) → project tut-claude-code-multi-engine, version 1
validate_project (projectId: tut-claude-code-multi-engine) → ok: true, 0 errors, 0 warnings; 4 scenes, 270 frames, 9 s, engines remotion, motion-canvas, html, hyperframes
render_project (projectId: tut-claude-code-multi-engine) → job job_mwqtqjjjfb5b2cd251: queued 0% (queued)
get_job (jobId: job_mwqtqjjjfb5b2cd251, waitSeconds: 45) → job job_mwqtqjjjfb5b2cd251: running 65% (render:s3: scene 3/4: 55/60 frames)
get_job (jobId: job_mwqtqjjjfb5b2cd251, waitSeconds: 45) → job job_mwqtqjjjfb5b2cd251: running 87% (assemble)
get_job (jobId: job_mwqtqjjjfb5b2cd251, waitSeconds: 45) → job job_mwqtqjjjfb5b2cd251: succeeded 100% (done), 270 frames, 9 s, 1080x1920
get_render_output (jobId: job_mwqtqjjjfb5b2cd251) → [poster image] render run_mwqtqjji30c1e03a60: 9 s, 270 frames, 1080x1920; files 7; download link (signed, masked)
The reel plays: 1080x1920, 270 frames, rendered in 107.6 s

agents-copy-snippet.proves: The /agents page gives a working Claude Code snippet: one click copies the `claude mcp add` command for the studio.

steps.text: Open /agents, the page that explains how an agent connects
Choose the Claude Code tab
Copy the snippet: the clipboard now holds the `claude mcp add --transport http reelforge …` command (the key stays a placeholder)
Scroll on to the per-agent keys and the example prompts

agents-copy-snippet.title: Connect Claude Code from /agents

commercial-purchase.proves: A buyer can pay for the Studio tier with Stripe (test mode), comes back to the order page with a Commercial licence key, and finds it in Dashboard > Licences.

steps.text: Open the pricing page as a visitor
Choose "Sign in to buy"
Signed out, so the button opens the hosted BuildBase sign-in page
Create a fresh test account (a +test address on the development environment)
Enter the verification code (test mode always accepts 424242)
Dismiss the optional prompt (passkey or two-factor offer)
Dismiss the optional prompt (passkey or two-factor offer)
Back on the store, signed in
Buy the Studio tier of the Commercial licence
Stripe Checkout opens (test mode)
Pay with the Stripe test card 4242 4242 4242 4242 (any future date, any CVC)
Paid: Stripe returns to the order page
The order page shows the Commercial licence key (masked here)
Dashboard > Licences lists the key, labelled Commercial

commercial-purchase.title: Buy a Commercial licence

personal-claim.proves: A visitor can sign up and claim the free Personal licence with no payment page, and the key shows on the order page and in Dashboard > Licences.

steps.text: Open the pricing page as a visitor: Personal is free, Commercial is a one-time licence
Choose "Get it free" on the Personal card
Signed out, so the button opens the hosted BuildBase sign-in page
Create a fresh test account (a +test address on the development environment)
Enter the verification code (test mode always accepts 424242)
Dismiss the optional prompt (passkey or two-factor offer)
Dismiss the optional prompt (passkey or two-factor offer)
Back on the store, signed in
Choose "Get it free" again: the claim needs no payment page
The order page shows the Personal licence key (masked here) with the noncommercial reminder
Dashboard > Licences lists the same key, labelled Personal

personal-claim.title: Claim a free Personal licence
